name: Cindergrain Godmask Devotional Coat
description:
A floor-length devotional coat worn by practitioners of the Meridian Convergence faith — a syncretic 2200 belief system blending West African Ifá, Japanese Shinto animism, and digital transcendence theology. The base is undyed heavy linen-analog in warm bone-white, hand-block-printed with interlocking Nsibidi script and circuit-path mandalas in iron-gall ink that darkens with age. Each coat is made by the wearer's shrine community, and the printing ceremony is itself a ritual act.

The back panel bears an embroidered 'godmask' — a geometric face assembled from both traditional masquerade forms and BCI port diagrams, symbolizing the divine as both ancient and networked. Sleeves have wide bell cuts to accommodate horn or wing geneware.
functionality: Wide bell sleeves accommodate wing and horn geneware; loose back cut fits spinal rigs; iron-gall printing becomes more distinctive with age and wear, marking long-term devotion.
what_it_says: You belong to something older and stranger than any corponation — and you are not afraid to say so in public.
worn_by: spiritual runners who tithe to the network
price_range: Not sold — gifted by community upon initiation
story_hooks: A Tier 5 corponation exec has been secretly attending Convergence shrines — someone spotted the coat under a concealment wrap and wants to know why.
A shrine's block-printing plates were stolen; without them, the next generation of coats cannot be properly consecrated, and the community is fracturing over what to do.
The BCI port diagrams embroidered into the godmask are real — traced from a proprietary neural architecture that should not be public knowledge.
